root_cause.text: btintel_hw_error() issues synchronous HCI commands via __hci_cmd_sync() without holding hci_req_sync_lock, allowing a race with btintel_shutdown_combined() (which runs under that lock) that concurrently accesses the same hdev->req_status/req_rsp, leading to a use-after-free when the close path frees the response SKB while the error path still references it.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "btintel_hw_error() issues two __hci_cmd_sync() calls ... without holding hci_req_sync_lock(). This lets it race against hci_dev_do_close() -> btintel_shutdown_combined(), which also runs __hci_cmd_sync() under the same lock. When both paths manipulate hdev->req_status/req_rsp concurrently, the close path may free the response skb first, and the still-running hw_error path hits a slab-use-after-free in kfree_skb()." The patch adds hci_req_sync_lock/unlock wrappers around the command sequence to serialize access.

Checks the result of the unprotected synchronous command; if another thread frees the skb concurrently, this check may access freed memory.
Frees the skb obtained from the unprotected __hci_cmd_sync; if another thread already freed it, this is a double-free; if another thread still references it, use-after-free occurs.
